policy_title: Restore International Development Spending for Climate Action
stated: Restore the UK’s role as a global leader on climate change, by returning international development spending to 0.7% of national income, with tackling climate change a key priority for development spending.

source.quote: Restore the UK’s role as a global leader on climate change, by returning international development spending to 0.7% of national income, with tackling climate change a key priority for development spending.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly directs UK international development spending toward climate action, directly affecting global emissions trajectories — the core measurable indicator for O6.

Restoring ODA from ~0.5% to 0.7% of GNI implies a material increase in public expenditure (circa £4–5bn/yr); whether funded or not, this is a non-negligible fiscal commitment that moves the debt-path sustainability indicator.

membership_note: Two fundamentals clearly bear: O6 (the stated climate purpose) and O12 (the fiscal cost of the spending restoration). Effects on O13 (global trade/stability) and O5 (security) are too diffuse and indirect to clear the non-negligible bar. O14 addresses domestic UK inequality, not global poverty, so it does not apply here.
